messages:
Sam Park: Heads up — saw a regression on canary around 09:02. P99 spiked ~30% when routing hit multi-variant fallbacks. Suspect batching slot fragmentation + kernel selection thrash.
Anya Patel: Noted. Which model mix? quantized variants + fp16 fallback?
Sam Park: Yeah — mix of q4_0 and fp16. When compat grouping misses we end up mixing kernels and the runtime chooses conservative kernels more often. KV cache miss rate also climbs.
Mohit Suresh: Do we have profiler traces? rough numbers?
Sam Park: Quick numbers from the profiler:
```
p99 latency: baseline 210ms -> canary 280ms
avg batch size: baseline 8.2 -> canary 5.6
kv_cache_hit: baseline 86% -> canary 67%
kernel_switch_count(per-epoch): +42%
```
Liz Chen: Oof. Kernel switches and smaller batches explain cost and latency. Any recent changes to token_budget or queue policy?
Sam Park: We pushed token_stride=32 -> 16 in the last rollout (to reduce tail latency). It reduced single-request latency but increased fragmentation across variants.
Anya Patel: If token_stride smaller, batches form more frequently with fewer tokens per slot -> number of cross-variant merges rises. That increases kernel selector churn.
Mohit Suresh: Hypothesis: we should try sticky-variant slotting for the first X tokens (e.g., reserve first slot variant affinity for 1s) to give KV cache time to warm and to allow compat grouping window to collect similar variants.
infra-bot: Deploy log: canary/slotting-experiment v2 rolled at 09:08 — config: {token_stride:16, compat_window_ms:120, slot_affinity_ms:0} :white_check_mark:
Sam Park: I'd like to run a controlled probe:
- set compat_window_ms to 200
- token_budget_target per-queue to 128 tokens
- enable soft-sticky-affinity for 250ms
Any objections?
Liz Chen: Sounds reasonable. Longer compat window should let batching coalesce similar variants. But watch queue latency tail — could increase for single-token requests.
Anya Patel: Also add a kernel-selection metric: capture % of batches that contain mixed-precision kernels and log kernel_map hashes. That will help confirm selector thrash.
Mohit Suresh: Agree. I'll add a simple probe patch to runtime:
```
metrics.emit("kernel_mix_pct", mixed_kernel_batches/total_batches)
metrics.emit("kernel_switches_per_min", switches/minute)
```
Sam Park: I ran a microbench locally with synthetic traffic (70% q4_0, 30% fp16) and soft-sticky 250ms: p99 back to 220ms, avg batch size 7.9, kv_hit 82%. Looks promising but need canary.
Anya Patel: Great. Two small failure modes to guard: (1) long affinity can starve low-volume variants -> set max_affinity_requests cap; (2) compat_window too long could delay first-token latency.
Sam Park: We'll cap affinity to 3 requests or 250ms whichever comes first. Implementing now.
infra-bot: Canary roll scheduled: slotting-probe-v3 -> 09:45, targets: 10% traffic, models: chat-x-variants.
Liz Chen: After ~30m canary, let's collect: kernel_mix_pct, kernel_switches_per_min, p50/p95/p99, avg_batch_size, kv_cache_hit. Also sample traces for mixed batches.
Mohit Suresh: If we still see >20% kernel_switch increase, next step is to bias the kernel selector: prefer quantized kernel when quantized variant majority >70% of batch. That trades some accuracy for latency/cost.
Sam Park: Good plan. Also thinking about an early fallback penalty: when a fallback occurs within first token of a request, flag and deprioritize immediate re-routing for 100ms to avoid rapid flip-flop.
Anya Patel: Add eval hook to measure output quality after any kernel-bias change — want to detect quality regressions quickly.
Liz Chen: Agreed. I'll coordinate the perf dashboard changes and the eval hooks.
Sam Park: Rolling out v3 now. Will post results in this thread in ~45min. :rocket:
